WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The first version chose, for every enzyme without
its own structure, the best hit of an RCSB sequence search, and recorded
the search score. That score was then read as "how close is this to my
enzyme". It is not: it ranks how well a hit matched the query, and six
enzymes scored 1.0000 against an entry that does not contain them.
Checking each entry against RCSB's own UniProt mapping shows that only
TWO of the 24 entries in enzymes.tsv hold the enzyme they stand for:
AS   3S9V -> Q38710  abietadiene synthase        correct
TS   3P5P -> Q41594  taxadiene synthase          correct
The other 22 are a different protein. Some are near relatives of the same
reaction type and were never going to be more than family-level evidence.
Others are a different enzyme altogether, and three of them matter most:
STS  -> 3A5S, which is BAS's own structure (Rheum benzalacetone synthase)
BAS  -> 1BI5, chalcone synthase, while BAS's own 3A5Q/3A5R/3A5S existed
LIC  -> 1N1B, bornyl diphosphate synthase, while a limonene synthase
structure (5UV1) was given to MYS and OCS instead
RNMT -> 5KOK, pavine N-methyltransferase, not reticuline N-MT
REPI -> 1ZGD, chalcone reductase, not reticuline epimerase
SQS  -> 3WEF, HUMAN squalene synthase, where the paper's SQS is the
Priestia megaterium enzyme (ADF40697)
This is also where the duplicate pairs came from: MYS and OCS were not two
paralogs legitimately sharing one structure, they were both assigned a
third enzyme. Predicting from each enzyme's own sequence removes the whole
class of error, which is why structure_source below prefers a model of the
right protein over a crystal structure of the wrong one.

HOLDING THE RIGHT PROTEIN IS NOT ENOUGH -- two further checks, added
2026-10-27, each of which changed an answer here:
COVERAGE. An entry can hold this protein and not hold all of it.
4CL's only experimental structure, 3TSY, is a 4CL::stilbene-synthase
FUSION at 3.1 A in which 4CL's last 102 residues were never modelled
-- and 4CL is an ANL-superfamily enzyme whose C-terminal domain closes
over the active site. A tunnel computed there would run out through a
hole where a domain should be and would look like a wide channel.
An entry needs >=90% of its aligned reference span observed and no
unobserved run longer than 30. Coverage is taken over the ALIGNED
span, not the whole UniProt length: 2ONG covers limonene synthase
57-599 because the transit peptide is cleaved, which is correct.
WHICH ENTRY, among several of the same protein. Coverage is a veto,
not a ranking. A bound cargo wins first (the start point comes from
where the channelled species sits), then wild type (an active-site
mutant is a different channel, which is why it was made), then
resolution. Taking the first cross-reference instead would give BAS
the apo 3A5Q over the holo wild-type 3A5R, and could give it 3A5S --
the I207L/L208F mutant, and the entry this set had already assigned
to STS by mistake.
AlphaFill now has to earn its place too: it outranks a plain model only
because a ligand-derived start point survives, so its best-identity
transplant must actually be usable (<=2.0 clashes per heavy atom, the
same threshold pick_ligands.py applies). Only the best-identity tier
counts -- accepting any usable transplant at any identity would be
picking by clash count, the trap pick_ligands.py exists to avoid. Over
the eleven candidates this changes exactly one answer: 4CL, whose ATP,
AMP and CoA all come from the tobacco homolog at 2.6, 4.1 and 4.4
clashes per atom.
OVERRIDE. 4CL is predicted with AlphaFold3 rather than taken from the
AlphaFold DB model the generic order would pick, because its channel
depends on an INTER-domain angle and that is the one thing this project
measured AF2 to be unreliable at. 3TSY stays in the record as a partial
cross-check: it cannot be the source, but it gives observed coordinates
for ref 22-459 to align the prediction against. Overrides live in
find_structures.py, never as an edit to this file -- this file is
generated, so a hand-edit to it is lost on the next run, silently.
IDENTITY IS NOT ONLY A UNIPROT QUESTION (added 2026-10-27). Four of these
enzymes have accessions UniProt does not index, so its curated PDB
cross-references could not answer and the code read "the authority cannot
answer" as "no structure exists" -- and predicted them. Comparing the
sequences directly, against the candidate entry each already had:
CUS   3ALE  100.0 % over 369 residues   -> its OWN structure. Switched.
GGPPS 2E8T  100.0 % over 335 residues   -> its own structure too, but
only 89 % of the span is observed, so the coverage veto
sends it to prediction with its site mapped from 2E8T.
CHS   1BI5   91.8 % over 389 residues   -> a close orthologue from
another plant, NOT the same protein. Prediction stands.
SQS   3WEF   32.8 % over 235 residues   -> distant. Prediction stands.
The 95 % bar is set so that CHS's 91.8 % does not pass; it was not chosen
to produce a wanted answer. GGPPS at 89 % coverage against a 90 % veto is
a genuine borderline and the threshold was deliberately NOT moved to let
it through: a discriminator was tried instead -- is the unobserved stretch
a folded domain or a disordered tail, by its pLDDT -- and it was REFUTED,
because GGPPS's missing 26 residues score 86.8 and 4CL's missing domain
87.5. No rule separates them, so the veto stands as written.
